question: Every year thousands of new US doctors are matched to hospitals. How is it done so that no pair would rather swap?
answer: By deferred acceptance, from David Gale and Lloyd Shapley in 1962. Applicants propose in order of preference; each programme holds its best offers so far and rejects the rest; rounds repeat until all settle. The result is stable: no doctor and hospital both prefer each other to their match. Shapley shared the 2012 Nobel prize.
move: A good matching leaves no pair who would both rather break away.
ask: Which arrangement around me leaves two people who would both rather swap?
source: The Nobel Prize, the Prize in Economic Sciences 2012
